title: Hybrid Search: Combining BM25 and Vector Search
description: Combine sparse keyword search (BM25) with dense vector search (HNSW) using score fusion and weighting in .NET.

data.text: For enterprise search, relying solely on dense vector search or solely on traditional keyword search leads to systematic retrieval failures. Keyword search (like BM25) excels at exact token matches—part numbers, error codes, legal statute numbers, and rare terminology—but fails completely when users employ synonyms or conceptual descriptions. Conversely, dense vector search understands conceptual context but frequently misses exact identifiers because embeddings compress tokens into generalized geometric representations.

data.text: Score Fusion Strategies: Convex Combination vs RRF
When combining sparse and dense results, search engines employ one of two strategies:

cards.title: Linear Convex Combination (Alpha Tuning)
cards.description: Calculates CombinedScore = (alpha * NormalizedVectorScore) + ((1 - alpha) * NormalizedBM25Score). Requires score normalization (e.g. MinMax or Sigmoid) because BM25 is unbounded while Cosine is bounded between -1 and 1.

cards.title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)
cards.description: Operates purely on ranks rather than raw scores: Score = sum(1 / (k + rank)). It does not require score normalization, making it robust against varying score scales across different search engines.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Hybrid search solves the precision blindspots of pure vector search and the vocabulary limitations of BM25
BM25 handles exact entity identifiers, codes, and domain acronyms with zero false positives
Dense vector search handles conceptual understanding, synonyms, and natural language phrasing
Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) merges rankings reliably without requiring complex score normalization
Enterprise search engines like Azure AI Search and Elasticsearch provide native hybrid pipelines out of the box
data.takeaway: Never deploy enterprise RAG with single-vector search alone. Combining BM25 keyword matching with dense HNSW vector search delivers the highest retrieval fidelity.
